title: Production verifier authority provider for the agent wrapper
description:
PREREQUISITE of task-97554aa4293e40eab56c0b642e18513a (Foundation self-host canary), discovered at the canary's step-1 resume-gate re-measurement on 2026-08-17.

MEASURED GAP at committed HEAD a42ae2f1f9168d13b8b786404fc47b366cc8edd9 (git grep against HEAD, not the working tree):

  git grep -n "verificationAuthority" HEAD -- apps/ packages/ | grep -v '\.test\.'
    apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper-main.ts:240:      verificationAuthority: () => null,
    apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/node-verifier.ts:62:  readonly verificationAuthority: (
    apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/node-verifier.ts:165:      const authority = config.verificationAuthority(nodeRef, brief);

  git grep -n "VerifierAuthorityFacts" HEAD -- apps/ packages/ | grep -v '\.test\.'
    -> only the type declaration (review/verifier-receipt-contracts.ts:15), its re-export
       (review/verifier-receipt-ledger.ts:22) and two consuming positions. ZERO producers.

THE DEFECT. The only production host that constructs the node verifier -- apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper-main.ts, the real `agent-wrapper-main.js` entry the canary must spawn -- passes `verificationAuthority: () => null`, with the shipped comment "No production authority provider is shipped yet. Refuse a green test rather than manufacture calibration, package or policy facts in-process."

node-verifier.ts:165-172 turns that null into, for EVERY node:
    reports.push({ detail: "host verifier authority unavailable", nodeRef,
                   outcome: "VERIFICATION_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE" });
    continue;

So `recordVerifierReceipt` (node-verifier.ts:176) is unreachable and the `integration.accept_output` dispatch (node-verifier.ts:152, :198) never fires through the production host. The refusal is honest and correctly fails closed -- this task is NOT a request to weaken it. It is the missing producer.

WHY IT BLOCKS THE CANARY. Canary DoD 3 requires one exclusive task to complete "plan, execute, verify, independent review, accept ... with exact receipts", and canary plan step 3 requires the journey to "execute the real verifier, independent review and final acceptance" through production surfaces. With no authority producer, the only reachable verify outcome is VERIFICATION_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE. Global rail Clause 2 forbids the alternatives: no narrowed DoD, no mock-backed journey, no authority reimplemented inside the E2E test.

Objective: ship the daemon-owned producer of `VerifierAuthorityFacts` and wire it into agent-wrapper-main, so a node with genuine durable calibration/package/policy facts verifies and earns a receipt, while a node WITHOUT them still refuses with the same stable outcome.

Deliverable: a focused daemon module (suggested apps/daemon/src/review/verifier-authority-provider.ts plus its one-line .js bridge) that reads the facts from the durable store -- never from caller input, never minted in-process -- plus focused tests; and the agent-wrapper-main.ts:240 edit replacing `() => null` with that provider.

NOT in scope: changing the VerifierAuthorityFacts shape, the receipt ledger, review-services acceptance, or anything under tests/e2e/foundation.

Read verifier-receipt-contracts.ts:15 for the exact required fields BEFORE planning, and confirm each field has a durable source; if any field has no durable source on disk, that is a further prerequisite to file, not a field to fabricate.
definitionOfDone: A production daemon module produces VerifierAuthorityFacts by reading the durable store; git grep shows it is the value passed at apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper-main.ts, and `verificationAuthority: () => null` no longer appears anywhere in production.

Every field of VerifierAuthorityFacts (per apps/daemon/src/review/verifier-receipt-contracts.ts:15) is sourced from a durable record; a test proves no field is defaulted, minted in-process, or read from caller input.

A test drives the real createNodeVerifier with the real provider over a seeded store and asserts a receipt was recorded via recordVerifierReceipt and the integration.accept_output dispatch fired -- asserting the receipt identity, not merely ok:true.
A test with the durable facts ABSENT asserts the literal outcome string VERIFICATION_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE and that no receipt row was written; the fail-closed path is preserved, not weakened.
A mutation drill on the provider's durable read makes the receipt-recording test go red for its receipt assertion (not for a crash), and production bytes are restored exactly.
pnpm typecheck and pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test are exit 0 with a nonzero printed Test Files count line; owned production files are each <=250 physical lines.
taskRails: Fail closed with stable reason codes; an absent durable fact stays VERIFICATION_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE and never gains authority by default.
Do not weaken or delete the existing refusal branch at node-verifier.ts:165-172; add the producer, keep the guard.
Use TDD. Keep each production source focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400.
Stage and commit only explicit owned paths by pathspec; no git add -A, no worktree, no push, no merge.

This is exactly the existing fixture relation in node-verifier.test.ts: seeded round items :60-68 minus the DAEMON_RECEIPT at :62 == AUTHORITY.packageItems :81-88. Not a fabrication - it is the contract's own "Host-owned package facts BEFORE the daemon appends its execution receipt" (verifier-receipt-contracts.ts:17).

(6) POLICY FIELD IS PolicyEvaluationInput, 13 EXACT keys (policy-validation.ts:159-163 INPUT_KEYS, enforced by exact() at :215) - NOT a PolicySlice. installPolicy:46 requires a `sliceRef` on the stored slice, so the durable slice = those 13 keys + sliceRef (14). (7) Calibration must be staleness CURRENT + sentinelPassed true + non-empty corpusRevision or qualifyReviewerForAcceptance refuses at ELIGIBILITY (reviewer-eligibility.ts:116-125). The provider does NOT enforce this - it returns what is durably stored and lets the kernel refuse; enforcing it in the provider would be a second source of truth.

implementationPlan.description: RED. Create apps/daemon/src/review/verifier-authority-provider.test.ts against a REAL SqliteEventStore on a temp file -- do not stub it. Seed durable state through PRODUCTION commands, not hand-written events: install the policy slice and the calibration slice via the real `policy.install` path, and record a review round via the real `review.submit` path so its package items are stored by the handler that stores them in production. Failing tests: (1) with all three sources seeded, `createVerifierAuthorityProvider({store, projectId})(nodeRef, brief)` returns a frozen `VerifierAuthorityFacts` whose `policy` equals the installed slice, whose `calibration` equals the installed calibration field by field, and whose `packageItems` are byte-identical to the stored bound items -- assert values, never `toBeTruthy`; (2) calibration slice absent -> `null`; (3) policy slice absent -> `null`; (4) the round's items ABSENT (`status: "ABSENT"`) -> `null`; (5) items PRESENT but their digest disagreeing with the round's stored `reviewInputDigest` -> `null`. Seed exactly ONE gap per case and assert the other four still return facts in the same file: because this port's only refusal channel is `null`, a suite that removes everything and asserts null passes even if the provider ignores the store entirely. Assert the raw event count is unchanged on every negative path.
implementationPlan.note:
RED verified twice, both for the right reason.

RED 1 (module absent): `npx vitest run --root . --config package.json src/review/verifier-authority-provider.test.ts` from apps/daemon ->

  Test Files 1 failed (1)
  Tests 4 failed | 6 passed (10)
  The 4 failures are exactly the POSITIVE controls, each "Error: expected durable authority facts, got null":
    - produces every fact from the durable store when all three sources are installed

10 cases, all seeded through PRODUCTION paths on a REAL file-backed store (`openRestartableStore()` -> `SqliteEventStore.openForProject` under a temp dir; no stub, no `:memory:`):
  - policy slice + calibration slice via `createDaemonCommandPorts(...).registry.get("policy.install")` and its decision port (the reviewer-calibration-record.test.ts pattern), capability project.admin, aggregate `${PROJECT_ID}-policy`;

Coverage beyond the plan's five, each justified in a file comment:
  (a) DAEMON_RECEIPT WITHHELD - measured in step-1 as binding: buildReviewPackage requires one in every stored round, recordVerifierReceipt refuses VERIFIER_AUTHORITY_REFUSED if the authority hands one back. Asserted as 6 host items, kinds excluding DAEMON_RECEIPT.
  (b) NON-DEFAULT CALIBRATION - installs {corpus-unlikely-7f,false,STALE} and asserts it reads back, so a hard-coded default (either the pessimistic UNKNOWN twin or an optimistic CURRENT one) cannot survive.
  (c) CALLER INPUT - two NodeMission briefs disagreeing in all four fields; results must be deep-equal.
  (d) ROUND SELECTION - an earlier ACCEPT round plus a later REJECT_IMPLEMENTATION round must yield null, pinning "the same round the receipt binds" (node-verifier.ts:137-138 takes rounds.at(-1) and requires ACCEPT; it does NOT search backwards).

Negatives seed exactly ONE gap and keep the other sources installed; each asserts `store.readEventsAfter` count is unchanged, so the provider is proven to perform no write on any refusal path.

implementationPlan.description: GREEN. Create apps/daemon/src/review/verifier-authority-provider.ts plus its one-line `.js` bridge (`export * from "./verifier-authority-provider.ts";` -- without it the module is invisible to the .js import graph). Export `createVerifierAuthorityProvider(config: {store: SqliteEventStore; projectId: string}): (nodeRef: string, brief: NodeMission) => VerifierAuthorityFacts | null`, matching `NodeVerifierConfig.verificationAuthority` (node-verifier.ts:62-65) EXACTLY so the call site needs no type change. COMPOSE the landed readers; do not reimplement them: `readReviewerCalibration` for calibration, and for the items read the review ledger for `nodeRef`, take the LATEST round (the same round node-verifier itself binds at :137-144, whose routing is ACCEPT), and pass its record to `verifyStoredPackageItems`. Bind the items ONLY from a verified result -- the digest comparison is the whole reason the items are trustworthy, so never read `record.packageItems.items` directly past it. Every returned object is `Object.freeze`d; any absent record, any refusal from either reader, and any thrown read returns `null` -- never a partial fact set, never a default. Perform NO writes. Keep the file <=250 physical lines; if the three reads push past it, split the readers into a sibling module rather than trimming a refusal branch.

apps/daemon/src/review/verifier-authority-provider.ts is 174 physical lines (<=250). Its .js bridge is the one line `export * from "./verifier-authority-provider.ts";`.

SURFACE: `createVerifierAuthorityProvider({projectId, store}): VerifierAuthorityProvider`, where `VerifierAuthorityProvider = (nodeRef: string, brief: NodeMission) => VerifierAuthorityFacts | null` — the exported TYPE is exactly NodeVerifierConfig.verificationAuthority (node-verifier.ts:62-65), so the wrapper call site needs no type change. The returned CLOSURE is declared `(nodeRef: string) => ...`, which is assignable to it: the brief is caller input, and a parameter that does not exist cannot be read by a later edit. Also exports VERIFIER_POLICY_SLICE_REF = "moe-verifier-policy/1", deliberately not 64 hex for the same reason REVIEWER_CALIBRATION_SLICE_REF is not.

COMPOSITION, no reader reimplemented:
- calibration: `readReviewerCalibration(store, projectId)`; any refusal -> null.
- policy: readDurableLedger -> stateOf(policyAggregateId) -> slices[VERIFIER_POLICY_SLICE_REF]. `installPolicy` requires a `sliceRef` on every slice and `validateEvaluationInput` accepts EXACTLY the 13 input keys, so the address is stripped and the remainder is handed to the CORE's own `evaluatePolicy` — admissibility is never restated locally. Then the four conditions decodeVerifierReceiptBytes:221-226 re-checks on read-back: ok, decision ALLOW, action integration.accept_output, actor NODE_VERIFIER_PRINCIPAL_ID. Refusing them here keeps them distinguishable; letting them through would flatten to VERIFIER_AUTHORITY_REFUSED with nothing left to say which failed.
- items: readReviewLedger(nodeRef); unreadable -> null; `rounds[rounds.length-1]` and routing must be ACCEPT — the exact selection node-verifier.ts:137-138 makes, NOT a backwards search for the newest clean round, because the receipt is keyed on that round's decisionId. The record then goes through `verifyStoredPackageItems`, and the items are bound from the VERIFIED result; `record.packageItems.items` is never read.
- the round's own DAEMON_RECEIPT is WITHHELD (filtered) — measured in step-1 as binding: buildReviewPackage requires one in every stored round, recordVerifierReceipt:178 refuses if the authority hands one back, and it appends the receipt for the run it just performed. These are the facts BEFORE that append.

FAIL-CLOSED: one refusal channel (null) for every cause; no partial fact set, no default, no `??` fallback, no spread over a partial object. A thrown read is caught and becomes null rather than an exception the verifier loop must interpret. NO WRITES — every negative test asserts the raw event count is unchanged — and no store handle is held past the call.

implementationPlan.description: RED then GREEN on the real composition, extending apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/node-verifier.test.ts (no parallel suite). Drive the REAL `createNodeVerifier` with the REAL provider over a seeded store -- no stub authority function in either case. Case A (earns a receipt): seed policy, calibration and an accepted round with stored items, supply a `runTest` returning `exitCode: 0` with a known output sha, and assert (i) the report outcome is exactly `"ACCEPTED"`, (ii) `readVerifierReceipt(store, projectId, verifierReceiptId(projectId, nodeRef, latest.decisionId))` returns `ok: true`, (iii) the stored receipt's `execution.outputSha256` equals the capture sha and its `calibration`, `policy` and `packageItems` are byte-equal to what the provider returned. Assert the receipt's identity and contents, not `ok: true` alone. Case B (fail-closed preserved): identical seeding minus the calibration slice; assert the report outcome is the literal string `"VERIFICATION_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE"`, that `runTest` was NEVER invoked (the authority check at node-verifier.ts:165 precedes the run at :173, and only a call-count assertion proves that ordering survived), and that no receipt row exists.

Wire the production host. In apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper-main.ts, replace `verificationAuthority: () => null` (at :280 as measured -- GREP for it, the line has already moved once) with the step-3 provider constructed from the wrapper's already-open `verifierStore` and `config.projectId`, both in scope at that point. Refuse a green test rather than manufacture calibration, package or policy facts in-process.") and replace it with one line stating that absent durable facts still yield VERIFICATION_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE -- the refusal is preserved, only its cause moves from "nothing is wired" to "nothing is installed". Prove the wiring by grep rather than by reading: `git grep -n "verificationAuthority" -- apps/ | grep -v '\.test\.'` must show the provider at the wrapper call site and must NOT show `() => null` anywhere in production.

Mutation drills, three, because 'the provider reads durably', 'it fails closed', and 'it trusts only verified items' are three separate claims a green suite cannot tell apart. Drill 1 (composition is real): make the calibration read return a hard-coded literal instead of `readReviewerCalibration`'s value; the step-4 Case A receipt-content assertion must go RED on the calibration comparison -- if it reddens on a crash or a different assertion, the test is not pinning the durable read. Drill 2 (fail-closed is real): make the absent-calibration branch return a fabricated facts object instead of `null`; the step-4 Case B assertion on the literal `"VERIFICATION_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE"` must go RED. Drill 3 (the digest gate is load-bearing): make the provider read `record.packageItems.items` directly, bypassing `verifyStoredPackageItems`; the step-2 case (5) digest-mismatch test must go RED. Record for each the command, the failing test NAME and the exact assertion. Restore by re-editing, never `git checkout` (destructive in this shared worktree), and confirm with `git diff --numstat` showing 0 added and 0 deleted per drilled file. One drill at a time -- a peer commit landing mid-drill can swallow the patch and leave git reading clean.

Adversarial self-review, then commit by explicit pathspec. Read the owned diff as an attacker: can any field of the returned facts originate from `NodeMission`, from a command payload, from a default or from a `??` fallback? Can items reach the facts without passing the digest comparison? Which ROUND's items are used -- is it provably the same round the receipt binds, or could a stale earlier round supply items for a newer decision? Does any negative path still permit a receipt? Does the provider write, or hold a store handle that outlives its call (a held SQLite handle kills the vitest worker)? Are `ReviewPackageBoundItem` values assignable to `ReviewPackageItemInput` without a cast that would erase the kind narrowing? Is the failure-round path at node-verifier.ts:88-98, whose `PACKAGE_ITEM_FILL` digests are synthetic by disclosed design, left untouched as it must be? Confirm no production file exceeds 250 physical lines. Then `git status --porcelain`, unstage any foreign entry with `git restore --staged -- <path>`, and commit ONLY these five paths by explicit pathspec: the provider .ts/.js/.test.ts, node-verifier.test.ts and agent-wrapper-main.ts. Verify with `git show --stat` that no foreign path appears; if a foreign whole-tree completion already captured these bytes, do NOT amend or reset -- record the merge-base diff for QA.

Verification gate. Run in the FOREGROUND, chained with `&&` so a red leg cannot be masked -- a `;` chain reports only the last command and a pipe reports the tail's exit code: `pnpm typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`. Read the OUTPUT, not the exit code: `pnpm --filter <pkg>` prints "No projects matched the filters" and EXITS 0 when the package name does not resolve, so the leg is evidence only if it prints a `Test Files N passed` line with N nonzero; `@moe/daemon` resolves to apps/daemon, and root `pnpm test` does NOT cover apps/** so it is no substitute. Repo-wide red is compared to the merge-base baseline and may be disclosed only when the new failing-path delta intersected with this task's five owned paths is empty; red inside the owned paths is a block, not a disclosure. In the completion note, name `task-97554aa4293e40eab56c0b642e18513a` as the consumer this unblocks -- closing GAP E of the Foundation self-host canary -- and state that GAP A remains open independently. This command's fresh output is the sole `complete_task` verification evidence.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: THIS PLAN REPLACES AN EARLIER ONE. The first attempt blocked correctly at its own step-1 gate: two of three VerifierAuthorityFacts fields had no durable writer, and the worker refused to mint six 64-hex digests from three scalars. That block was right, and it also caught an architect error -- my original notes claimed package items were derivable from `readReviewLedger`, when `submitRound` was discarding them. Both gaps are now closed by task-5edf037f (calibration) and task-92031b0a (package items), so the provider is buildable from real durable sources and this plan composes them. REJECTED NOW: (a) reimplementing either reader inside the provider -- both are landed public surfaces and a local copy would drift and then police the copy rather than production; (b) reading `record.packageItems.items` directly -- it is reachable and typechecks, but it skips `verifyStoredPackageItems`, which is the only thing making stored items trustworthy; drill 3 exists to catch exactly that shortcut; (c) widening the port to return a diagnostic refusal code instead of `null` -- `NodeVerifierConfig.verificationAuthority` is node-verifier's contract and the task rails put it out of scope, so the tests carry the discrimination instead by seeding one gap at a time; (d) defaulting any field -- see the risks; a legal-but-unproven calibration is the single most dangerous wrong answer here and the landed reader already refuses rather than synthesising one.

planningNotes.risks: The single most dangerous wrong answer is a synthesised absent calibration: `{corpusRevision:"", sentinelPassed:false, staleness:"UNKNOWN"}` is a legal ReviewerCalibration that reviewer-eligibility maps to REVIEWER_CALIBRATION_UNPROVEN, so returning it LOOKS fail-closed and passes a careless review while asserting a calibration exists when none does. The landed reader already refuses instead; the provider must propagate that refusal as null and never rebuild the value. Second, the port's only refusal channel is `null`, so a negative suite that removes everything and asserts null passes even against a provider that ignores the store -- seed exactly one gap per case and keep passing controls in the same file. Third, `record.packageItems.items` is reachable and typechecks without the digest check; bypassing `verifyStoredPackageItems` yields items that are present but unattested, which is precisely the authority-without-evidence failure epic rail 4 forbids -- drill 3 pins it. Fourth, ROUND SELECTION: the provider must bind the same round the receipt binds (node-verifier takes the latest round whose routing is ACCEPT at :137-144); silently using an earlier round would attach stale evidence to a newer decision and every assertion would still pass. Fifth, ordering: the authority check precedes runTest, so Case B must assert runTest was never called or a reordering regression stays green. Sixth, line numbers have already moved once between plans -- grep, never trust them. Seventh, close every SqliteEventStore handle on every path; a held handle kills the vitest worker. Finally, leave node-verifier.ts:88-98 alone: its PACKAGE_ITEM_FILL digests are synthetic by disclosed design and out of scope.
